what: Input pipeline latency of a DJI FPV Remote Controller 3, Gamepad API vs WebHID, on a local release drawing scan 39e63ce9 in this PC's Chrome at its 30 Hz display (the owner's item 7). Fake controller in the page: the roll stick changes at known moments E; per edge: delivery = first arrival in FlightSession.input - E, stamp = the page time the physics applies it at - E, frame = first animation frame at or after the arrival - E (ms). busy25: 25 ms of main-thread load per frame. Control hid-late20: 20 ms of added dispatch delay must show as ~20 ms more delivery.

findings: Superseded (review R3): the first runs' "Gamepad 0.9 vs WebHID 3.6 ms" and "stamp error 0 / 0" came from unequal fakes; the numbers below are from equal fakes (section review).

The gamepad is not polled once per display frame (a 500 Hz loop). With the same device on both paths (a report every 6 ms) at the owner's 30 Hz: a change reaches the page in 5.6 ms (p50, p90 9.7) on the Gamepad API path and 3.4 ms (p90 5.5) on WebHID; the ~2 ms is the browser's 4 ms provider tick, as modelled. Within a few ms on fakes; the real paths need the real controller.

The physics stamp (when the move is applied in sim time): Gamepad API 2.8 / 4.8 ms (p50 / p90) after the move, the report's own arrival (half the report period); WebHID 3.4 / 5.5 ms. Under 25 ms of main-thread load per frame the gamepad stamp stays 3.1 / 5.1 ms (before the fix it was the delivery, 20.6 / 30.9 ms), because it is Gamepad.timestamp: this holds only if Chrome's Gamepad.timestamp is the arrival time on the page clock (Chromium sets it when the report is processed; the page-clock conversion was not checked on the owner's Chrome; when it is not plausible the poll time is used, as before).

OPEN: the WebHID path, the DJI's primary button, still applies inputs late under load: stamp 15.5 / 29.7 ms (p50 / p90) with 25 ms of load per frame, because its stamp is the inputreport event's timeStamp, which in the fake is the main thread's dispatch; whether Chrome stamps a real report at arrival or at dispatch was not checked, and the page has no earlier time for a WebHID report. Under load the Gamepad API path is the better-timed one.
Controls fired: hid-late20 +21.4 ms delivery (20 added); gamepad-lag8 +7.7 ms stamp and +8.8 ms delivery (8 added): the stamp follows Gamepad.timestamp.
What the pilot sees is bound by the display: the first frame that can show a change comes 22-27 ms after it (p50) on this 30 Hz display on both paths; the display then adds its own scan-out.
Not measurable here: the DJI controller's own delay between a stick move and its USB report, and Chrome's real gamepad thread timing; both need the real controller (and a camera or a photodiode).

review.why: v0.8 review R3: the first runs compared unequal fakes (a gamepad with no report period whose Gamepad.timestamp was the edge time E itself, against a HID device with 6 ms reports), so their 0.9 vs 3.6 ms and their 0 / 0 stamp error came from the fakes. Rerun with the same device on both paths (a report every 6 ms) and the pad modelled on Chromium's gamepad code (Gamepad.timestamp = the arrival of the report, the page sees it at the provider's next 4 ms tick).
review.build: local release of cf81fbb (review fixes; devices/gamepad.ts unchanged since d11e7ed)
